title: Early drummers: foot pedals, tuning drums and reading drum music
summary: Dawson says drummers always had pedals, tuned their drums to a trumpet note, and few could read drum music, apart from Joe Welch.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did they have, uh, two drummers in those times? I mean, before they had the foot pedal, do you remember them? Yeah. Tom Albert told me about it. They always had foot pedals?
Oh, all the time. They always had foot pedals. One guy played a snare drum, played a bass drum, at the same time.
Tom Albert told me about that, you know, when he was young.

I know, uh, that they had something at that time when I was playing. And they had a drummers. Mm-hmm. Used to tune, tune the drummer up. Mm-hmm. By the band. They had a note. They had a certain note that the trumpet player could make. Yeah. And that note, the drummer could catch it and tune up from that, that note he made on the corner.
You're a drummer. You should ask him some questions about drumming.

And, uh, at a tune, the snare would have the proper tone, and the bass drum would get the proper tone. Cause, cause he'd run it up. And it would, it would be sharp or flat. He could tune it up, you see, until he'd get to the right pitch. And then, we had drummers, we had very few drummers at that time that could read music. Mm-hmm. Now, that's Brother Joe Welles, he could read drum music. Yeah, he was a good little drummer. We had very few drummers that could read music. Drum music, that I'm talking about. Yeah.
